title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. K is a number field, T_K = R_{K/Q} G_m and V_K = Ker(N_K : T_K → G_m), the norm-one torus. E_K is the unit group, and F is its image in V(R). The goal, completed on the next page, is to build a torus S_K^0 = T_K/R and an exact sequence 1 → V'_K → S_K^0 → G_m → 1, where V'_K is the largest quotient of V_K that is compact over R (anisotropic over R) and in which the units have finite image. This is the connected Serre group attached to K.

Top of page, end of a proof of (i)⇔(iii). By Dirichlet's unit theorem the units give a discrete subgroup of rank r1+r2−1 in V(R), so V(R)/F is compact. The torus generated by V(R)/F is then compact, and so is the quotient V'_R it generates. A crossed-out attempt at (iii)⇒(i) writes V'(R) as a quotient of (R_{>0})^{r1+r2−1} × (Z/2)^{r1} × U^{r2}.

Main argument, (iii)⇒(iv).
1. Choose a finite Galois extension K̃ ⊃ K over Q, with G = Gal(K̃/Q). Let I_K = G/Q be the set of embeddings K → Q̄. The character group of T_K is Z[I_K] as a G-module. The constant functions give Z ⊂ Z[I_K], and these are the characters factoring through the norm.
2. A quotient V' of V_K corresponds to a G-submodule N with Z ⊂ N ⊂ Z[I_K]; the characters of V' are M = N/Z.
3. V'_R is compact exactly when complex conjugation τ acts on M by −id. Then τ is central in the image of G in Aut(M). Hence M is a module over G' = G/P, the largest quotient of G in which τ is central. So P is the normal subgroup generated by the commutators [τ, g].
4. P acts trivially on N/Z and on Z. Since P is finite, it acts trivially on N. Therefore N ⊂ Z[I_K]^P = Z[P\I_K].
5. Since P is normal, P\I_K = G/PQ = I_L, where K' = K̃^P and L = K ∩ K'. So N ⊂ Z[I_L], and V' is dominated by V_L via the norm N_{K/L}.

Interpretation. K' is the largest subfield of K̃ in which complex conjugation is central, i.e. the maximal CM or totally real subfield. So L is the maximal CM or totally real subfield of K, and L_0 = L ∩ R is its maximal totally real subfield.

Previous page. V_{L_0} is R-split, while V_L/V_{L_0} ≅ U^r is compact.

Next page (Corollary 2). This gives V_K^cpct ≅ V_L/V_{L_0}, with R = Ker(N_{K/L})·V_{L_0}. The character group of S_K^0 consists of the Σ n_σ[σ] supported on I_L with n_σ + n_{τσ} constant. This is the Serre condition, i.e. infinity-types of algebraic Hecke characters.
errors: The crossed-out line writes R^{*+(r1+r2-1)}; this should be (R_{>0})^{r1+r2-1}, i.e. R^{*}_{+}. It is only a notational slip in a deleted passage.
The step 'P acts trivially on N/Z, hence on N' needs a short justification that is not written: a finite group acting unipotently on a lattice acts trivially. The step is true.
Identifying Z[I_K]^P with Z[P\I_K] via orbit sums is implicit but correct. The note also uses P\I_K = G/PQ, which requires P to be normal; P is normal as defined.

ideas.what: Largest R-compact quotient of the norm-one torus V_K whose character module satisfies τ = −1 on N/Z. It is computed via the largest quotient of Gal in which complex conjugation is central, which yields the maximal CM subfield L of K: V_K^cpct ≅ V_L/V_{L_0}.
ideas.modern_name: Connected Serre group S_K (Serre torus); its character group is the set of infinity-types n_σ with n_σ + n_{τσ} constant, supported on the maximal CM subfield
ideas.usually_credited_to: J.-P. Serre, Abelian l-adic representations and elliptic curves (1968), Ch. II; later Deligne/Milne–Shih in the CM-motive and Taniyama group context
ideas.where_published: Serre 1968 Ch. II; Milne–Shih in Deligne–Milne–Ogus–Shih LNM 900 (1982)

ideas.what: The units are cocompact in the norm-one torus over R (Dirichlet), and the finiteness of the units' image in a compact quotient.
ideas.modern_name: Dirichlet unit theorem; Zariski closure of the units
ideas.usually_credited_to: Dirichlet; Serre for the use in defining S_K

ideas.what: Maximal subfield of a Galois closure in which complex conjugation is central, equal to the maximal CM-or-totally-real subfield.

missed.claim: Historical point. In a manuscript catalogued as 'Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965)', Grothendieck independently derives the structure of the connected Serre group S_K^0 = T_K/R. He gives the CM-subfield description R = Ker(N_{K/L})·V_{L_0} and an exact sequence 1→V'_K→S_K^0→G_m→1, evidently as the motivic Galois group of CM/abelian-type motives. This is possibly before or parallel to Serre's 1967–68 McGill exposition. The archive dating ('1965–[vers 1977]') makes priority uncertain.
missed.quote: N ⊂ Z[I_K]^P = Z[P\I_K] ... Or P\I_K = I_L, donc ... N ⊂ Z[I_L], ce qui signifie que le quotient V' de V_K est majoré par V_L.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is relevant to the history of how the Serre group entered the theory of motivic Galois groups and the Taniyama group. The mathematics itself is now standard.

deep.surprise_reason: The computation is correct and is exactly the standard description of the Serre torus via the maximal CM subfield. Its only interest is historical: it shows Grothendieck working this out inside the motivic Galois theory notes, with uncertain dating.
transcription_corrections: 'G'=G/P' in the margin: P is the normal subgroup generated by the commutators of τ (so τ is central in G'). The crossed 'H' in 'H opère trivialement' should be read as P.
'K' est Weil[?]' is likely 'K' est le plus grand sous-corps ... où τ est central' (CM); the reading 'Weil' is doubtful.
